what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat several conditions. It can relax overactive muscles to help with crossed eyes (strabismus), uncontrolled blinking (blepharospasm), abnormal head and neck movements (cervical dystonia), arm stiffness after a stroke (upper limb spasticity), and leg stiffness. It is also used to prevent chronic migraines (15 or more headache days per month), treat an overactive bladder or bladder leakage caused by nerve damage, reduce heavy underarm sweating (hyperhidrosis), and treat certain eyelid spasm conditions. A separate cosmetic form is used to temporarily smooth frown lines and wrinkles on the face.
how_to_take: This medicine is NOT a pill or liquid you take by mouth. It is given as an injection directly into muscles, glands, or the bladder wall by a trained healthcare provider such as a doctor or nurse. You will receive this treatment in a clinic or doctor's office. Do not try to inject this medicine yourself at home. The number of injections and the exact spots where they are given will depend on the condition being treated. Stay calm and let your provider know if you feel any discomfort during the procedure.
dosing: The dose is different for every person and every condition. Your doctor will decide the right dose, the number of injections, and how often you need treatment. Most treatments are repeated every 3 to 6 months, but this can vary. For chronic migraine prevention, injections are usually given every 12 weeks. For overactive bladder, injections may be given every 6 months or as needed. Never ask for a higher dose or more frequent treatments on your own, as too much of this medicine can be dangerous.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic, you will not accidentally miss a dose at home. However, if you miss or need to reschedule your appointment, call your doctor's office as soon as possible to set up a new time. Try not to wait too long between treatments, as your symptoms may return or worsen. Do not try to 'make up' for a missed treatment by getting a double dose at your next visit.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home because it is prepared and given by your healthcare provider. If for any reason you are handling it, know that unopened vials must be stored in a refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep it away from light and do not freeze it. Once the vial is opened and the medicine is mixed (reconstituted), it should be used within 24 hours. Always keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin or aspirin, because they can increase bruising at injection sites. Avoid alcohol for at least 24 hours before your injection to reduce the chance of bruising. Do not rub or massage the treated area for at least 24 hours after your injection, as this can spread the medicine to nearby muscles and cause unwanted effects. Avoid strenuous exercise and lying down flat for 4 hours after facial injections. Tell your doctor if you have received any other botulinum toxin product recently, as combining them can increase the risk of serious side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room right away if you notice any signs that the medicine may have spread beyond the injection site. These serious warning signs include trouble swallowing, speaking, or breathing; muscle weakness all over your body; double vision; drooping eyelids; loss of bladder control; or feeling faint. These effects can happen hours to weeks after your injection. Also call your doctor if you have signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; if you develop a urinary tract infection or have trouble urinating after a bladder injection; if you have severe pain or unusual bruising at the injection site; or if your symptoms do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Most people start to notice improvement within 1 to 3 days after their injection, but it may take up to 2 weeks to feel the full benefit. The effects of the medicine are temporary. They usually last about 3 to 6 months, depending on the condition being treated and the individual patient. When the effect wears off, your symptoms may gradually return, which is why repeat treatments are scheduled. Results can vary from person to person.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established and it is generally not recommended. If you are elderly, you may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, so your doctor may start with a lower dose. Children: this medicine is approved for certain conditions in children as young as 2 years old, but the dose will be carefully calculated based on your child's weight and condition. If you have a neuromuscular disease such as ALS, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome, tell your doctor before receiving this medicine because you may be at higher risk for serious side effects including severe muscle weakness and breathing problems. If you have had trouble swallowing or breathing in the past, make sure your doctor knows before starting treatment.
